title: Codebook diversity loss
goal:
Implement the diversity loss $\mathcal{L}_d$ of Section 3.2 (Equation 4).

Write `diversity_loss(logits)`. `logits` has shape `(N, G, V)`: for each of `N` time steps, `G` codebook groups with `V` entries each. Compute the softmax over the `V` axis (no Gumbel noise, no temperature), average it over the `N` steps to get $\bar p_{g,v}$, and return

$$\mathcal{L}_d = \frac{1}{GV} \sum_{g=1}^{G} \sum_{v=1}^{V} \bar p_{g,v} \log \bar p_{g,v}$$

It is the negative entropy of the averaged distribution, summed over groups and divided by `G * V`. Use the natural logarithm.
hints: A stable softmax subtracts the maximum over the last axis first.
Average the probabilities over axis 0, not the entropies. A codebook that picks one different entry at every step has a uniform average even though each step is certain.
Entries with $\bar p = 0$ contribute 0 because $x \log x \to 0$. Use `np.where(p > 0, p * np.log(p), 0.0)` or add a tiny constant inside the log.
